selected_dataset.name: Wearable Device Dataset from Induced Stress and Structured Exercise Sessions
selected_dataset.license: Open Data Commons Attribution License v1.0

selection_reasons: The stress cohort contains 36 healthy volunteers, larger than WESAD's 15-subject cohort.
The Empatica E4 provides EDA, skin temperature, and three-axis acceleration, enabling a shared-feature external test of subject baseline normalization.
The protocol contains baseline, rest, cognitive-stress, and social-stress blocks with event tags and self-reported stress levels.
The archive is openly licensed, versioned, DOI-addressed, and small enough for local deterministic validation.
The dataset was collected independently of WESAD with a different device placement and protocol.

pre_outcome_scope.primary_comparison: subject-disjoint raw representation versus per-subject median/IQR-normalized representation
pre_outcome_scope.secondary_comparison: calibration informativeness and worst-subject coverage reported jointly with accuracy and full-set frequency

known_quality_constraints.S02: Duplicated stress-session signals; exclude from the primary complete-case cohort unless exact truncation can be independently verified.
known_quality_constraints.f07: PPG and temperature sensors were covered; exclude from the primary all-shared-modality cohort.
known_quality_constraints.f14: Stress session split into baseline and protocol files; exclude from the primary complete-file cohort, retain for a separately validated sensitivity analysis if merge timing is unambiguous.

freeze_sequence: Validate ZIP central directory, CRCs, safe paths, size, and expected inventory.
Extract without overwriting an existing validated dataset.
Build a subject/session/tag inventory without computing scientific outcomes.
Freeze exact exclusions, stage intervals, minimum window counts, folds, and effect-size decision rules.
scientific_guardrails: This dataset is an independent cohort and protocol, but its stress recordings are not necessarily multi-day repeated sessions.
Device placement differs from WESAD, so feature definitions will be shared at the summary-statistic level rather than assumed sensor-equivalent.
Protocol labels and self-reported stress are distinct outcomes and will not be silently conflated.
No outcome will be calculated before the exact analysis protocol is frozen from the validated inventory.
Failure to replicate normalization will weaken generality rather than invalidate the WESAD result.
